solved.q: Find the order and degree of the differential equation: d^2y/dx^2 + (dy/dx)^3 = 0
steps: The equation is already a polynomial in derivatives, so no squaring/removal of radicals is needed.
Highest derivative present is d^2y/dx^2, so order = 2.
Power of the highest order derivative d^2y/dx^2 is 1, so degree = 1.

solved.q: Find the order and degree of the differential equation: sqrt(1 + (dy/dx)^2) = d^2y/dx^2
steps: The equation has a radical, so first remove it by squaring both sides.
Squaring: 1 + (dy/dx)^2 = (d^2y/dx^2)^2
Now it is a polynomial in derivatives.
Highest derivative present is d^2y/dx^2, so order = 2.
Power of the highest order derivative is 2, so degree = 2.

solved.q: Solve the differential equation: dy/dx = x^2 y
steps: Using variable separable method, separate the variables y and x on opposite sides.
dy/y = x^2 dx
Integrating both sides: integral of (1/y) dy = integral of x^2 dx
Taking exponential on both sides: y = e^(x^3/3 + c) = A e^(x^3/3), where A = e^c

solved.q: Solve the differential equation: dy/dx = (1 + y^2)/(1 + x^2)
steps: Using variable separable method, separate the variables.
Integrating both sides using the standard formula integral of 1/(1+t^2) dt = tan^-1(t) + c
tan^-1(y) = tan^-1(x) + c

solved.q: Solve the homogeneous differential equation: dy/dx = (x^2 + y^2)/(xy)
steps: Since the equation is homogeneous of degree 0, put y = vx, so dy/dx = v + x(dv/dx).
So v + x(dv/dx) = (1 + v^2)/v
Separating variables: v dv = dx/x
Integrating both sides: v^2/2 = ln|x| + c
Substitute back v = y/x: (y/x)^2 / 2 = ln|x| + c
Multiply both sides by 2x^2: y^2 = 2x^2(ln|x| + c)

solved.q: Solve the homogeneous differential equation: dy/dx = (x + y)/x
steps: RHS can be written as 1 + y/x, which is a function of y/x, so the equation is homogeneous.
Put y = vx, so dy/dx = v + x(dv/dx).
v + x(dv/dx) = 1 + v
x(dv/dx) = 1, so dv = dx/x
Integrating both sides: v = ln|x| + c
Substitute back v = y/x: y/x = ln|x| + c
Multiply both sides by x: y = x ln|x| + cx

solved.topic: Linear differential equations and integrating factor
solved.q: Solve the linear differential equation: dy/dx + y/x = x^2
steps: The equation is of the form dy/dx + Py = Q with P = 1/x, Q = x^2.
Integrating factor, I.F. = e^(integral of P dx) = e^(integral of 1/x dx) = e^(ln x) = x
General solution of linear DE: y . (I.F.) = integral of Q . (I.F.) dx + c
y . x = integral of x^2 . x dx + c = integral of x^3 dx + c
xy = x^4/4 + c

solved.topic: Linear differential equations and integrating factor
solved.q: Solve the linear differential equation: dy/dx + 2y = e^(-x)
steps: The equation is of the form dy/dx + Py = Q with P = 2, Q = e^(-x).
Integrating factor, I.F. = e^(integral of 2 dx) = e^(2x)
General solution: y . e^(2x) = integral of e^(-x) . e^(2x) dx + c
y . e^(2x) = integral of e^x dx + c = e^x + c
Dividing both sides by e^(2x): y = e^(-x) + c e^(-2x)

solved.q: Form the differential equation by eliminating the arbitrary constant A from y = A e^(2x)
steps: Given y = A e^(2x) ... (1)
Differentiate both sides w.r.t. x: dy/dx = 2A e^(2x)
From (1), A e^(2x) = y, so dy/dx = 2y

solved.q: Form the differential equation representing the family of lines y = Ax + B, where A and B are arbitrary constants
steps: Given y = Ax + B ... (1)
Differentiate w.r.t. x: dy/dx = A ... (2)
Differentiate (2) again w.r.t. x: d^2y/dx^2 = 0
This removes both arbitrary constants A and B.

solved.q: The population of a town grows at a rate proportional to the population present (dP/dt = kP). If the population doubles in 5 years, find the population after 10 years, in terms of the initial population P0.
steps: Using the law of growth, dP/dt = kP leads to P = P0 e^(kt) by variable separable method.
Given P doubles in 5 years: 2P0 = P0 e^(5k)
So e^(5k) = 2, giving k = (1/5) ln 2
After 10 years: P = P0 e^(10k) = P0 (e^(5k))^2
solved.ans: P = 4P0 (population becomes 4 times the initial population)

solved.q: A body cools from 80 degree C to 60 degree C in 20 minutes in a surrounding of constant temperature 30 degree C. Using Newton's law of cooling, find the temperature of the body after a further 20 minutes (i.e., 40 minutes from the start).
steps: By Newton's law of cooling, dT/dt = -k(T - Ts), whose solution is (T - Ts) = (T0 - Ts) e^(-kt)
Here T0 = 80, Ts = 30, so T - 30 = 50 e^(-kt)

practice.q: Find the order and degree of: (d^3y/dx^3)^2 + (dy/dx)^5 = 7
practice.hint: No radicals/fractional powers present; order = power of highest derivative term index, degree = power of that highest derivative.
Separate variables as dy/y = tan x dx and integrate using integral of tan x dx = ln|sec x| + c.
Put y = vx, dy/dx = v + x dv/dx; this reduces to cot v dv = dx/x.

practice.topic: Linear differential equations and integrating factor
practice.q: Solve: dy/dx + y cot x = cos x
practice.hint: Here P = cot x, so I.F. = e^(integral cot x dx) = sin x; multiply and integrate using integral of sin x cos x dx = sin^2(x)/2.

practice.q: Form the differential equation by eliminating the arbitrary constants A and B from y = A cos x + B sin x
practice.hint: Differentiate twice; note y'' = -(A cos x + B sin x) = -y.

practice.q: Form the differential equation by eliminating the arbitrary constant c from xy = c
practice.hint: Differentiate using the product rule: d/dx(xy) = x(dy/dx) + y.

practice.q: A radioactive substance decays according to dN/dt = -kN with half-life T. Find the time taken for the substance to reduce to one-fourth of its original amount.
practice.hint: Use N = N0 e^(-kt) with k = ln2 / T; one-fourth means two half-lives have passed.

practice.q: A bacteria culture doubles every 3 hours. Find the time required for the culture to become 5 times its original size.
practice.hint: Use P = P0 e^(kt) with e^(3k) = 2, so k = (ln2)/3; solve e^(kt) = 5 for t.
